_comment: Dead-end reverse proof (owner 2026-10-28) on hp_1015_carved.pcd (map frame, m): a 0.75 m wide corridor (inner faces x = -0.375, 0.375) from y = -1.30 (the mouth, 1.3 m ahead of the takeoff spot, so the robot sees the floor in front of it on the way in: a reverse uses observed floor only) to an end wall at y = -3.60, straight ahead of the takeoff spot (0, 0, yaw -90.7: facing map -y). Walls 0.06 m thick, 0.8 m high: above the track planner's band. The robot drives in (dead_end_reverse.yaml leg 1), then gets a goal behind it: no room to pivot in 0.75 m (the pivot circle is 0.78 m across at pivot_margin 0.05). 0.75, not the owner's 0.70: the track planner's 0.1 m cells and the render's returns (<= 0.05 m in front of a surface) make a 0.70 m corridor ~0.60 m between occupied cell centres, under the frame plus margins (0.557 m): the robot cannot drive into it (d14), so it must back out to the mouth (l4_track::plan_reverse), pivot there and drive on.
